html:
The People's Republic of the Congo was the Marxist-Leninist state proclaimed in Brazzaville on 31 December 1969 by Captain Marien Ngouabi, the first in Africa to call itself that.

It had one party, the Congolese Party of Labour, a red flag and close ties to the Soviet Union and Cuba, while oil was still pumped by the French company Elf. Rivalry between officers from the north and politicians of the south ran through it. Ngouabi was assassinated in 1977, and from 1979 Denis Sassou Nguesso led the state.

Debt and the end of the Cold War brought it down. A national conference in 1991 stripped the party of power, and in 1992 the country held multiparty elections and dropped the name. Its army and militias fought again in the civil war of 1997.
sum: The People's Republic of the Congo was the Marxist-Leninist state proclaimed in Brazzaville on 31 December 1969 by Captain Marien Ngouabi, the first in Africa to call itself that.
